item.title: Enugu Corps member’s death not caused by substandard medicines – NAFDAC
item.description: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has debunked reports that a Corp member whose death occurred in Enugu died of effects of substandard and falsified medicines. This is contained in a statement by the Director-General of the agency, Prof Mojisola Adeyeye, in Abuja on Friday. The statement noted that the deceased Corp member previously at NYSC Orientation Camp, Awgu, in Enugu State, did not die of what people insinuated. According to the statement, preliminary investigations revealed that the Corp member was brought to the Camp clinic aided by two other Corp members on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at about 9:00pm with symptoms suggestive of severe malaria and a known peptic ulcer disease patient. The statement stated that the deceased was however, stabilised with intramuscular antimalarial and other supportive medications given intravenously. It stated that the deceased was placed on bed rest for observation till Oct 8 morning when he was discharged with oral medications. “He came back unaided on Saturday, Oct. 10, with complaints of right thigh pain for which he was asked to see a physiotherapist. “His profuse sweating caught the attention of the medical doctor, who measured his blood pressure and found it to be low (80/40 mmHg). He was stabilised with intravenous Normal Saline. “Serial monitoring showed recurrent episodes of hypertension. item.title: DSS, military, police arrest 5 over NYSC members kidnap
item.description: …As 3 others escape with gunshot injuries By Soni Daniel Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), the military and police have arrested five suspected members of a criminal gang allegedly responsible for the abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members in Imo State on Nigeria’s 66th Independence Day. Five other suspected members of the gang, however, escaped with gunshot injuries prompting a massive manhunt for them. The suspects were apprehended during a series of intelligence-led operations conducted at different locations in Rivers and Abia States. However, in the course of the operation, three other suspects escaped with varying degrees of injury. Security sources disclosed that the operations were carried out between October 10 and 14 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State and Aba South LGA. Abia State. Recall that 20 NYSC members were abducted by armed men along Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, as they travelled to their assigned orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The victims were subsequently rescued on October 7, 2026, during a joint security operation at Amakohia Ubi Village. The string of operations mark a significant breakthrough in efforts to track down the perpetrators, dismantle the criminal network allegedly responsible for the abduction and bring those involved to justice. A security source described the development as a major relief, noting that security agencies had sustained a wide-ranging manhunt for the abductors. “This is a huge sigh of relief. Security agencies have been on a manhunt for the abductors, and we are elated that they have been captured. We strongly believe they will be charged to Court by DSS and the corps members will get justice,” the source said. item.title: NSIB probes private jet after door falls mid-air
item.description: A private jet operated by Triton Aviation made an emergency landing at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, after losing a door mid-air on Thursday. The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) confirmed the incident to TheCable on Friday, saying an investigation had commenced. “The incident happened yesterday and investigations are ongoing,” a source at the bureau said. According to a report by Punch on Friday, the aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI and flight identification DWC052, was heading to the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, when the incident occurred at about 4:20 pm. Citing an incident report, the publication said the aircraft was about three nautical miles from the airport and climbing through 3,000 feet when the crew issued a distress call. “Mayday, Mayday, Mayday,” the crew reportedly transmitted. Following the distress call, airport fire and emergency personnel, alongside the medical team, were alerted and placed on standby. Fire and rescue teams were also directed to designated positions in preparation for the aircraft’s return. The report further stated that at about 4:29 pm UTC, while communicating with the Abuja control tower, the crew asked whether air traffic controllers could confirm if the door was open. “The duty air traffic controller attempted to observe the aircraft using binoculars, but could not establish the door’s condition because of the aircraft’s position. The crew was subsequently informed that the controller could not confirm the situation visually,” the report said. The aircraft subsequently landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 4:34 pm UTC, about 14 minutes after the Mayday call. Following the landing, the duty controller reportedly observed that the aircraft’s door was missing from the fuselage. The jet was then taxied to the international apron extension and parked with the assistance of a marshaller. Meanwhile, a video circulating on social media showed what appeared to be an aircraft door lying on farmland near Abuja. According to Billionaires.Africa, the NSIB confirmed that the door had been recovered. “The door has been recovered and secured at the NSIB wreckage hangar,” the bureau said. The NSIB said it had commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and would provide updates as the investigation progresses. On accountability, Pate said the Federal Government was collaborating with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) to track health sector funds and prevent their misapplication. “Government will not condone any act that is capable of depriving ordinary Nigerians of the health goods these funds are meant for,” he said. item.title: Iran denies Saudi accusation of involvement in Houthi attacks
item.description: Iran on Friday denied having anything to do with attacks by Yemen’s Houthis, a day after Saudi Arabia accused it of having encouraged the group’s recent escalation against the kingdom. Since Yemen’s civil war flared back to life in July, the pro-Iran Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week. A Saudi-led military coalition has supported Yemen’s internationally recognised government for more than a decade, and reported on Friday having intercepted more missiles and drones as the kingdom comes under sustained attack from the Houthis. A day earlier, a Saudi foreign ministry official said Iran had “encouraged” the escalation, which Tehran denied. “The Islamic Republic of Iran rejects any claim that Iran has played a role in Yemeni (Houthi) operations,” Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a statement. “Yemen’s armed forces act according to their own interests and assessments, and such claims are not credible to those familiar with relations between Iran and its friends. Nevertheless, Iran does not consider an escalation of tensions to be in the interests of any party,” he added. The Saudi official, deputy minister for public diplomacy Dr. Rayed Krimly, had said the Houthis rejected an offer to meet in Oman at the outset of the latest round of hostilities. Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani, disclosed this on Friday while commissioning a telecommunications tower under the National Universal Communications Access Programme (NUCAP) in Bende, Abia State. item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu’s nominee for chairman of the board of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC), Abdullahi Saidu, has told the Senate that the commission has operated without a board for more than 13 years, a situation he said has hindered its operations. Saidu spoke on Wednesday when he appeared before the Senate Committee on Finance for screening alongside six other nominees. He said the absence of a board had left the commission with significant institutional challenges, adding that the incoming board would have to rebuild its operations if confirmed. Saidu said the commission was expected to establish offices in at least one location in each of the six geopolitical zones but currently operated only from Abuja. He pledged to work with the National Assembly and other stakeholders to strengthen the commission and improve its capacity to discharge its mandate. The nominee also disclosed that the commission lacked prosecutorial powers, explaining that it could investigate cases and forward its findings to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice for prosecution. He said the proposed board would seek a review of the law establishing the commission to strengthen its independence and operational capacity. Saidu further pledged to improve government revenue by strengthening the monitoring of operating surpluses generated by government-owned and other organisations covered by the commission’s mandate. According to him, some revenue-generating organisations fail to remit the appropriate share of their operating surpluses to the Federal Government. He said such organisations were expected to remit 80 per cent of their operating surpluses to the Consolidated Revenue Fund while retaining 20 per cent for their operations. “Because the commission is not informed, so they just declare whatever they feel they want to declare,” he said. Saidu assured the committee that, if confirmed, the board would strengthen monitoring to ensure that the appropriate revenues were declared and remitted. He expressed confidence that the commission’s performance could improve within a year, provided it received the necessary support from the National Assembly and other stakeholders. The screening was presided over by Senator Lere Oyewumi, vice-chairman of the committee, who represented its chairman, Senator Sani Musa. Addressing the nominees, Oyewumi said managing the commission required specialised knowledge and preparation, noting that the assignment differed from other public service roles. He urged them to participate in retreats with experts and undertake extensive reading to prepare for the responsibilities ahead. Senator Osita Ngwu, representing Enugu West, moved a motion for Saidu and the other nominees to take a bow and leave, while Senator Sadiq Suleiman Umar, representing Kwara North, seconded the motion. item.title: NSIB Probes Mid-Air Door Separation On Aircraft En Route To Lagos
item.description: The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) says it has launched an investigation into the separation of an aircraft door involving a Challenger 604 operated by Triton. In a statement, the Bureau said the aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI, was flying from Abuja to Lagos when its crew declared a mayday after the door separated at an altitude of 3,500 feet. The aircraft subsequently returned to Abuja and landed safely on Runway 22. All nine persons on board, comprising three crew members and six passengers, were accounted for. The NSIB said the separated door had been recovered and secured as investigators began work to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The Bureau said further updates would be provided as the investigation progresses. The post NSIB Probes Mid-Air Door Separation On Aircraft En Route To Lagos appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Kenya Records Third Ebola Case, Health Ministry Says
item.description: Kenya has recorded its third case of Ebola, a close relative of the country’s first two Ebola cases, the health ministry said on Friday. The country had not reported a single case of the contagious virus until last week, after a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) died after returning to Kenya. Just over a week later, a second man, a relative of the first, also tested positive for the virus while in quarantine. The DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak in May. The deadly disease has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years. The 65-year-old woman was a “primary contact and a close relative of the first and second cases”, the ministry said in a statement, adding that she had been in quarantine since October 6. A Kenyan Ministry of Health official checks the temperature of a traveller at the Busia One Stop Border Post (OSBP) on the Kenya-Uganda border as health authorities step up Ebola screening measures, in Busia on October 12, 2026. Photo by BRIGHT EMOJA / AFP After developing symptoms, including “fever, sore throat and malaise”, she was isolated and tested positive for the virus. The ministry emphasised that the risk to the public “remains low” and there was “no evidence of community transmission”. It said of 130 contacts, 127 had been traced and were in quarantine, with efforts “ongoing to trace and quarantine the three remaining contacts”. On Wednesday, the ministry confirmed its second case, a 39-year-old relative of the first victim, stating he was in isolation and there was “no evidence” of any large-scale transmission of the virus. The country has never previously reported a case. Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 people infected, almost all of whom had travelled from the neighbouring DRC, and two deaths, before being declared Ebola-free in August. Kenya’s first victim was a national, who has not been named but was referred to as a 40-year-old businessman. He fell ill around a month ago and had been treated in the DRC, before travelling overland to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, and flying into Nairobi on October 3. He was hospitalised in Nairobi but died on October 5, according to Health Minister Aden Duale. According to Congolese health authorities, the outbreak has infected 9,066 people so far and caused 4,381 deaths since the emergence in the DRC of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment. The suspension takes effect on Saturday, October 17, 2026, with the resumption of full clinical duties, following government commitments to address the doctors’ demands.
